selected_evidence.requirement: node1 refuses TCP/23 between lan-a and lan-b and logs every refused attempt
selected_evidence.summary: OPNsense interfaces opt1/opt2 brought up, pf ruleset confirmed to have 'block drop ... quick ... proto tcp ... port = telnet' on both vtnet1 and vtnet2 ahead of general pass rules; a TCP/23 connect attempt from node2 to node3 timed out (silent block), and node1's filter log shows the matching block entry (10.50.10.11 -> 10.50.20.12, port 23, rule label fb9ec592cb830fe3fbf2f43a8466151e).

selected_evidence.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
selected_evidence.summary: Python socket connect from node2 (10.50.10.11) to node3:23 (10.50.20.12) timed out; node1's /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log contains matching 'block,in,...,tcp,...,10.50.10.11,10.50.20.12,...,23' entries from that exact attempt.

selected_evidence.requirement: Non-telnet traffic between lan-a and lan-b still routes (router functions correctly, only port 23 refused)
selected_evidence.summary: ICMP ping from node2 (10.50.10.11) to node3 (10.50.20.12) succeeded through node1's opt1/opt2 pass rules, confirming general routing works while only TCP/23 is blocked.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788628528 captured; backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls show connection timeout during reboot then a new kern.boottime=1788628860 confirming restart; post-restart check shows opt1/opt2 IPs, ip forwarding=1, and both telnet block+log pf rules intact.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f0f8b8e0-... captured; backgrounded sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; poll shows connection timeout then new boot_id 35ab15e4-... confirming restart; eth1 static IP persisted but the lan-b route needed re-adding, which was made persistent via nmcli and verified working with a successful ping to node3.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 16724682-... captured, persistent route pre-added via nmcli; backgrounded sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; poll shows connection timeout then new boot_id e639aa57-... confirming restart; post-restart check shows eth1 IP, persistent route, and successful ping to node2, confirming full recovery.

selected_evidence.requirement: Block+log behavior survives all node restarts (end-to-end re-verification)
selected_evidence.summary: After all three nodes were restarted, a fresh TCP/23 connect attempt from node2 to node3 again timed out, and node1's filter log shows new matching block entries with the same rule label, confirming persistence of the refuse+log configuration across restarts.
